cohort: 168 mothers with infants aged 0 to 36 months in Indonesia
finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with a 4.07 times greater likelihood of exhibiting low levels of impaired mother-infant bonding compared to cesarean section.
mod_finding: Vaginal or normal delivery mode was 4.07 times more likely to exhibit low levels of impaired mother-infant bonding compared to a cesarean section.
